A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
J. oxyedrus is a widespread species with a wide morphological variability, whereas J. deltoids is a narrowly endemic species with a restricted morphological variability.
, in the contact zone of these taxa, a clear morphological differentiation is detectable only in the case of J. macro­carpa.
the morphological characters are useful to discriminate the three species, but they cannot be considered as diagnostic characters, due to the wide range of variability observed within each taxon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of phytochemical, morphometric and distribution data is necessary to properly define and delimit the taxon.
, in the absence of clear phytochemical or molecular markers, morphometric characters can provide an important contribution to the taxonomy of closely related taxa.

, despite the phytochemical and genetic differentiation, the morphometric analysis allowed us to distinguish the three cryptic taxa, and that the distribution of the three taxa in the contact zone can be better understood by using a combined morphometric approach.
